name: App windows
summary: For a VM with a display: its programs open as windows on the Mac. Builds Monad's window manager in the VM, and adds a terminal (foot) to start with.

steps.title: A C compiler and a terminal
Monad's window manager
steps.script:
# The VM's programs as windows on the Mac (the VM's Display setting): Monad's
# own window manager, built here from the sources Monad's installer puts in a
# VM whose Display is on, with the VM's C compiler (Monad ships no program
# for Linux it did not build). Its service takes the display in place of the
# Desktop profile's session.
lib="$MONAD_ROOT/usr/local/lib/monad"
# The installer runs at each boot, about when this does: it may still be at it.
n=0
while [ ! -e "$lib/wm-build" ] && [ "$n" -lt "${MONAD_WM_WAIT:-60}" ]; do
    sleep 1
    n=$((n + 1))
done
if [ ! -e "$lib/wm-build" ]; then
    echo "Monad has put no window manager in this VM. It does for a VM with a display: turn on Display in the VM's settings in Monad, restart it, and set this profile up again." >&2
    exit 69
fi
sh "$lib/wm-build" "$lib" || exit $?
mkdir -p "$MONAD_ROOT/etc/profile.d"
cat > "$MONAD_ROOT/etc/profile.d/monad-windows.sh" <<'EOF'
# Monad: a program started from a tab opens as a window on the Mac, while
# the VM's window manager is there.
if [ -S "${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/run/user/$(id -u)}/wayland-0" ]; then
    XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/run/user/$(id -u)}"
    WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0
    XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland
    MOZ_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1
    QT_QPA_PLATFORM="wayland;xcb"
    export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR WAYLAND_DISPLAY XDG_SESSION_TYPE MOZ_ENABLE_WAYLAND QT_QPA_PLATFORM
fi
EOF
systemctl daemon-reload
# One of the two has the display.
systemctl disable --now monad-display.service 2>/dev/null || true
systemctl enable monad-wm.service
# A VM without a display (Display is off in its settings) keeps it for when it has one.
if [ -e "$MONAD_ROOT/dev/dri/card0" ]; then systemctl restart monad-wm.service; fi
